sentences.text:
Gagan Parashar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 August,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:17245
 1 M
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta

On The 8 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 33596 of 2025
 Gagan Parashar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:

Bal Krishna Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner [P-1]
 Dinesh Savita appearing on behalf of Advocate General[
 Order

This is third application filed under Section 483 of BNSS and 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail to the applicant in connection with Crime No.386/2021 registered at Police Station - Kolaras District Shivpuri(M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 201, 120- B of IPC and Section 13(1)(ka), 13(1)(kha), 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.
2. According to the prosecution case, Tau (elder brother of fathe rof applicant) is public servant being employee of the bank.
It is alleged that total amount of Rs.80 crores has been embezzled.
Some amount (Thirty two lac) was transferred in the account of applicant and by utilizing the aforesaid embezzled amount, applicant has also purchased the land.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
Applicant is under custody since NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:17245 2 MCRC-33596-2025 11.09.2024.
His first bail application M.Cr.C.No.55914/2024 was dismissed on merit vide order dated 06.01.2025.
His second bail application was dismissed on merit by a common order of present applicant and co-accused Smt. Reena Yadav passed in M.Cr.C.No.13436/2025 and M.Cr.C.No.12971/2025 dated 9.05.2025.
After the dismissal of the second bail application, co-accused Smt. Reena Yadav has been granted bail by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Special Leave Appeal (Crl.)No.9056/2025 dated 21.07.2025.
Counsel for the applicant submits that the case of present applicant is similar to the case of co-accused Smt. Reena Yadav.
Therefore, he prays for grant of bail on the ground of parity.

sentences.text: 4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6 . Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the aforesaid co-accused has been granted bail by the Apex Court, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One lac Only) with two solvent sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court.
7.
In case, if he is found involving in offence of the same nature, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without further reference to the Bench.

v) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and vi) The applicant will not leave India without the previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
8. Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
9. E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.
